coverage_note: Accessible national runoff releases reviewed through 13 October; coverage is not certified exhaustive. Registration numbers are transcribed from reports, not independently verified in PesqEle.

polls.notes: Historical wave. Keep in trend; latest-per-pollster aggregation uses the 12 October wave instead. Mobile and landline IVR interviews.

Original release linked an older PDF; the newest report was identified in the 13 October roundup. The '-1' filename suffix alone does not establish a substantive revision. Published full response categories sum to 101% due to rounding.

Fieldwork 8, 9 and 12 October, per primary report; some secondary coverage said 9–12. Published valid base is 2,314 of 2,400. Use published 55/45, not the ratio of rounded total shares. Earlier 2/3 October releases shared 1,250 interviews and are not included.

Primary report gives 10–12 October, not 9–12. Valid shares here are 48/(48+45) and its complement. Some secondary coverage reports 52/48, but the retrieved primary text did not expose that valid-vote table. Registration transcribed, not independently verified.

PDF is a printout of the Folha release. Sample of 2,520 across 153 municipalities. Exact interview locations not confirmed from retrieved primary text. Source update timestamp does not establish a numerical revision.

Valid shares are derived from rounded total shares: Flávio 42.7/86.9=49.1369%; Lula 50.8631%. These are not pollster-published valid figures. Stratified probabilistic household sampling is claimed by the source.
Use all-elector valid results 52.7/47.3, not the maximum-turnout subset 53.1/46.9. Total response categories sum to 101% due to rounding. n=1,500 fails both 2,000 sample filters.

Exactly 2,000 respondents: excluded by >2,000, included by ≥2,000. NS/NR is inconsistent: summary p4 says 2%, main chart p12 says 1%; leave undecided missing. Main valid chart p13 gives 53.1/46.9; summary rounds 53/47.

Fieldwork straddles the 4 October first round; excluded from the strict baseline. Do not split its 3.2% combined residual into invented undecided/blank components. Primary report was retrieved; candidate-chart pixels were not independently visually verified in the source review.

Released 13 October; newly verified and added 14 October. Primary report pages 4, 10 and 12 visually verified. Published all-elector valid shares 51.8/48.2; valid-response sample not reported. Exactly 2,000 interviews: excluded by >2,000, included by >=2,000. This round changes schooling weights from TSE to PNAD Continua/IBGE (report p5). PDF metadata retains an older title; cover, registration, fieldwork and charts identify October 2026 round 1. Registration transcribed, not independently verified.

Original Broadcast release by Isadora Duarte and Geovani Bucci, syndicated on VIVA on 15 October at 09:18 Brasilia. National all-elector runoff; published valid shares 51/49, not a derivation from rounded totals. Total shares 44/42; 8% say they will not vote, separately from 4% blank/null and 2% undecided/do not know. Valid-response sample not reported. Exactly 2,000 interviews. Registration transcribed, not independently verified.

Complete original PoderData report embedded by CNN Brasil resolves the initially missing national total-vote shares. Original release still links the prior wave; current report cover, registration, fieldwork and technical sheet identify this wave. Totals 47/47, blank/null 4 and undecided 2; published valid shares 50/50. Mobile and landline IVR; 644 municipalities in all 27 federation units. All electors aged 16+, with demographic and declared first-round vote weighting. Valid-response sample count not reported.

Round172 original CNT report: actual sample2014 in140 municipalities, superseding advance announcements of2002. National full-electorate stimulated runoff results; socio-economic and declared first-round vote weighting. Published valid shares50.5/49.5; total shares46.8/45.9, blank/null4.9, undecided2.4. Valid-response sample count not reported. In-person household and intercept interviews; confidence95%.

polls.mode: In person at population flow points
polls.notes: Results first released 15 October; full institute report and technical article available 16 October, resolving the earlier hold. The report and institute explicitly confirm fieldwork 13-14 October, ending on the afternoon of 14 October, and 2,520 in-person interviews in 153 municipalities among national electors aged 16+. This supersedes the 13-15 October wording in the earlier rejection news article. Published valid shares 51/49; chart p9 states 2,330 valid-vote interviews, while the cross-tab appendix labels its 2,335 base as weighted. Report pp2,8,9 visually verified. Registration transcribed, not independently verified.

Second weekly runoff wave, released 17 October. Full national electorate aged 16+, CATI interviews 13-15 October; 1,500 respondents. Report page5 publishes all-elector valid shares 51.2/48.8 and rounded stimulated totals 48/46, blank/null3 and undecided3. Use the published valid shares rather than renormalizing rounded totals. Page13 separately reports a maximum-turnout subgroup at 52.2/47.8; this subgroup is excluded. Valid-vote base count not reported. n=1,500 fails both 2,000 sample filters. Registration transcribed, not independently verified.

Released 18 October; national electorate, in-person household interviews 15-17 October, n=2,100, 95% confidence. The complete 53-page institute report is hosted by CNN. Page13 publishes stimulated all-elector totals Lula46.4/Flavio44.6, nobody/blank/null5 and undecided3.9 (99.9 from rounding), and valid shares Lula51.0/Flavio49.0. Use published valid shares; valid-vote base count is not reported. Page7 spontaneous responses (50.6/49.4 valid) and demographic subgroups are excluded. The October9 wave is retained as history. Registration transcribed from the report, not independently verified.

Released 19 October. National Atlas/Bloomberg report, fieldwork 13-18 October, n=4,998, Atlas RDR online recruitment with demographic and previous-vote poststratification, 95% confidence. The report calls its target the Brazilian adult population and shows age bands starting at 16; the national runoff charts use the full sample. Visually verified pages 7-8 give total Flavio 49.8/Lula 47.6 and published valid 51.1/48.9. Combined blank/null/dontknow 2.6 is not split into invented components. Valid-response sample count is not reported. The October 9 wave and its original chart caveat remain unchanged. Registration transcribed from the report, not independently verified.

Released 19 October, 18th wave. National electors age 16+, fieldwork 16-18 October, n=2,002, telephone CATI, 27 federation units, 95% confidence. Complete 128-page original BTG/Nexus report resolves the prior missing-primary hold. Visually verified page 22 gives stimulated full-sample totals Flavio 46.5/Lula 45.9, nobody/blank/null 4.7, NS/NR 2.9; page 24 explicitly publishes stimulated valid 50.3/49.7. Published valid values are used; valid-response count is not reported. Methodology introduces one-decimal reporting; the page 25 historical chart has inconsistent spontaneous/stimulated question labeling, so the prior October 13 wave and its denominator caveat remain unchanged. Registration transcribed, not independently verified.

Released 19 October. National electors age 16+, fieldwork 16-18 October, n=3,000 across 695 municipalities in 27 federation units; mobile/landline IVR/URA, 95% confidence. Complete 33-page original PoderData/Aya report. Page 7 national total columns give Flavio 49/Lula 46, blank/null 4, dontknow 2 (sum 101 from rounding); page 11 publishes valid 52/48, excluding blank/null and dontknow, as a survey projection distinct from actual ballot-valid votes. Published valid shares are used; valid-response count is not reported. Technical sheet notes approximate margin given telephone-list coverage and weighting. Prior waves retained; registration transcribed, not independently verified.

Released 19 October. Complete 18-page Futura/100% Cidades report, third October round, fieldwork 16-17 October, n=2,000 national electors aged 16+, telephone CATI, margin 2.2pp at 95% confidence. Visually verified pages 4, 10 and 12: full-sample stimulated totals Flavio 48.3/Lula 47.5, nobody/blank/null 2.4 and NS/NR/undecided 1.9 (rounding sum 100.1); explicitly published valid shares 50.4/49.6. Valid-response sample count is not reported. Page 5 discloses education weighting moving from TSE to PNAD Continua/IBGE; this source-method change is documented without changing aggregation assumptions or historical rows. Earlier Futura October 16 release remains held for its own fieldwork-date conflict; this new report consistently states October 16-17. Registration transcribed from report, not independently verified.

Original release 19 October; newly verified from the complete 38-page DataTrends primary report linked by the 20 October Poder360 national roundup. National electors aged 16+ with a voter registration and eligible to vote; 2,000 automated telephone URA/DTMF interviews, 15-17 October, margin 2.19pp at 95% confidence. Pages 4 and 12 report full-sample Flavio 49%, Lula 46%, none/blank/null 4%, and NS/NR 1%; pages 4 and 13 explicitly publish valid-vote shares 51.5/48.5, excluding residual responses. Retain published valid shares rather than recomputing from rounded total percentages. Exact candidate-valid respondent count is not reported; 2,000 valid interviews is the full eligible sample, not the candidate-valid denominator. Source weighting uses UF, sex, age, education and income; source DEFF diagnostics do not replace the frozen model assumptions. The earlier missing-primary-report hold is resolved by this complete report, while its historical record is retained. Registration transcribed from report, not independently checked in the TSE registry.

Complete 48-page primary report: national electors, 2,000 interviews, fieldwork 15-19 October, released 20 October 2026. Telephone interviews with human interviewers; initial recruitment used telephone calls and virtual messages. Margin 2pp at 95% confidence. Stimulated runoff on page8 reports Flavio48%, Lula45%, blank/null5%, NS/NR2%. Pages15-16 explicitly publish valid-vote shares52/48; use those published shares rather than normalizing rounded48/45. Spontaneous47/44 results on page6 are a different question and are not substituted. Exact candidate-valid respondent count is not supplied and remains null. No turnout-restricted universe is stated. Registration transcribed from report, not independently checked in the TSE registry.

Verified from complete HTML releases by TMC, whose polling partnership is documented on Alfa Inteligencia official site. Main release20October07:30(updated07:41) reports stimulated national runoff totals Flavio48.8%, Lula45.9%, blank/null3.5%, undecided1.8%; explicitly published valid shares51.5/48.5 exclude residual responses. Same-wave companion methodology confirms2700 national electors aged16+, five regions, personal interviews15-19October, margin1.9pp at95% confidence, BR-00820/2026. Exact candidate-valid respondent count unavailable; valid_base_n remains null. Use published valid shares, not normalization of rounded totals. CNN-hosted PDF remains above the30MiB capture cap and was not used, compressed, truncated or repackaged. HTML source verification does not certify the inaccessible PDF. Earlier PDF-size hold and acknowledgment remain historical audit records. Registration is transcribed, not independently verified against TSE.

Verified from complete original HTML release and companion by Fonte83, the named Data Ranking polling partner. Published20October, fieldwork14-16October2026, national electors16+ in urban/rural areas across five regions;2100 personal household interviews with structured questionnaire and cluster sampling using sex, age, schooling and income. Technical methodology specifies2.15pp at95% confidence under simple random sampling, without cluster design effect; introductory two-point description is rounded. Use the explicit technical2.15pp, while frozen model design effect remains unchanged. Published valid shares are Flavio49.6/Lula50.4 excluding blank/null/neither6% and undecided4%; total shares44.6/45.4. Candidate-valid respondent count not provided; valid_base_n null. Companion confirms same registration and national figures. Main result image returned403 and was not retried or used; complete HTML independently states all required fields. No linked full PDF located. Registration transcribed, not independently checked with TSE.

Complete original 59-page Meio/Ideia report and publisher release dated 21 October 2026 reviewed. National electors aged 16 or older, telephone RDD with probability proportional to size; fieldwork 15-19 October, n=1500, 95% confidence and 2.5pp maximum margin under simple random sampling. Published valid shares 51.1% Flavio / 48.9% Lula on page 6; total shares 48% / 46%, blank/null 3.4%, do not know 2.6% on page 7. Candidate charts visually verified. Published valid shares retained rather than recomputed from rounded totals. Valid-vote respondent count not explicitly supplied; valid_base_n remains null and subgroup counts are not substituted. Page 58 defines national population 16+ and sampling/weighting; no turnout-only restriction found. Registration transcribed, not independently checked in TSE registry. Public report and full original article accessible without submitting forms or bypassing access controls.

polls.mode: Online non-probability survey recruited through social-media advertisements
polls.notes: Complete original 112-page Wave 8 report and three-page release reviewed. National all-electorate question, entire n=5000 sample, ages16+, online non-probability recruitment; fieldwork18-20October, released21October. Pages23-24 visually confirm rounded totals Flavio50%, Lula48%, blank/null/or would not vote1%, undecided0%; zero is explicitly published and does not imply no undecided respondents. Rounded totals sum99%; report page8 and release explain rounding. Valid shares derived as50/(50+48), not published valid shares; valid respondent count unspecified. Full report pages12,14,16,20 and release headers identify BR-04612/2026; release opening paragraph retains conflicting BR-09028/2026, treated as an editorial carryover because full technical report and current-wave headers independently agree. Registration not independently verified against TSE. Report specifies maximum sampling MOE2.4pp,95% confidence, effective Kish n1745 and unequal-weight effect2.86; these do not cover selection/coverage error. Fixed aggregator methodology unchanged; retain actual sample5000, do not substitute effective n or pollster weight effect. Wave8 uses same v3 calibration as Wave7; earlier missing-evidence wave remains separately held.

Full authoritative HTML release and methodology reviewed, corroborated by original Globo release21October10:16Brasilia. National all-electorate stimulated runoff, ages16+, n2154, household in-person fieldwork17-20October. Total shares45/44, blank/null/will not vote9, undecided2. Valid shares derived45/(45+44), not published Quaest valid shares or a likely-voter projection; valid respondent count unspecified. MOE2pp at95% confidence. Registration reported by sources, not independently verified in TSE. Original institute PDF not retrieved. Use explicit field dates; TVT entirely-after-debate wording conflicts with17October start and its rejection bullet reverses prior/current values; these non-model assertions are not used. Prior-wave verification holds remain unchanged.

Released 21 October. Complete 18-page Futura/100% Cidades report, fourth October round, fieldwork 19-20 October, n=2,000 national electors aged 16+, telephone CATI, margin 2.2pp at 95% confidence. Visually verified pages 4, 5, 10 and 12: full-sample stimulated totals Flavio 48.9/Lula 46.8, nobody/blank/null 2.0 and NS/NR/undecided 2.3; explicitly published valid shares 51.1/48.9. Valid-response sample count is not reported. Page 5 repeats the education-weighting disclosure from TSE to PNAD Continua/IBGE already present in earlier Futura rounds; not treated as a newly dated methodology break. Aggregation assumptions and historical rows unchanged. Registration transcribed from report, not independently verified.
